newsitem.title: FINLAND: POHJOLA CEO SEES TRIPLING LIFE INSURANCE.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA CEO SEES TRIPLING LIFE INSURANCE.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola expects its life insurace business and the Finnish market for life insurance to triple in the next 10 years, CEO Iiro Viinanen told a news conference on Thursday.

Life insurer Suomi and its subsidiary Salama are currently an unconsolidated part of Pohjola group and Pohjola said earlier on Thursday it would concentrate its life insurance operations into its public part.
"We have roughly three billion markka (annual premium income) in Suomi-Salama, this could cautiously estimated triple in the next 10 years," Viinanen said.
Pohjola now has about 30 percent of the Finnish life insurance market, he added.
Viinanen said the concentration of life insurance operations was prompted by the market's prospective strong growth.
